title: Mo's Quiet Turn
learning_objectives: Explain why Mo stops guessing even though he knows the answer.
Connect Mo's wish to act with his idea of guessing objects.
parent_prompts: Before reading: In a game where one friend acts and the other guesses, which job would you like to try first?
After page 4: Mo knows the answer but stays quiet. Why? Which words tell you what he wants?
After reading: Compare the first animal turn with the umbrella and teapot turns. What changes, and which rule stays the same?

pages.text: Rain taps the window. Sam wants a game without pieces, so he suggests guessing pretend animals.
pages.image_alt: Sam sits on a coral rug facing Mo, the round yellow bird, with open palms and rain on the window behind them.

pages.text: Sam bends his knees and makes a trunk with his arm. Mo guesses elephant. Next, Sam waddles like a penguin.
pages.image_alt: Sam bends his knees, raises one arm from his shoulder to his nose, then lets the forearm hang and curl like a trunk. Mo watches with an open beak.

pages.text: Mo knows the answer, but he stays quiet. He wants to act instead of always guessing.
pages.image_alt: Sam takes a short waddling step with bent knees, feet turned outward and arms held like short wings. Mo stands with a closed beak and one wing lifted.

pages.audio_script: Mo knows the answer, but he stays quiet. He wants to act instead of always guessing.

pages.text: Mo points to himself, eager for a turn. Sam remembers the two jobs and invites Mo to act.
pages.image_alt: Sam kneels and holds out an inviting hand while Mo touches his own chest with one yellow wing.

vocabulary.definition: Asks someone to join in or do something.

pages.text: Mo curves both wings above his head, then slowly opens them. This time, he is not an animal.

quiz.prompt: Why does Sam suggest an animal guessing game?

options.text: He wants to play without pieces
The rain has spoiled his cards
Mo has asked to play it

quiz.explanation: Page 1 says Sam wants a game without pieces, so he suggests guessing pretend animals.

quiz.prompt: Why does Mo stay quiet during the penguin turn?

options.text: He needs a harder animal clue
He wants the rain to stop
He wants a turn at acting

quiz.explanation: Page 2 gives acting and guessing as the two jobs. Page 4 says Mo knows the answer but wants to act instead of always guessing.

quiz.prompt: Which plan matches Mo's wish and new idea?

options.text: Taking acting turns and guessing only animals
Taking acting turns and guessing objects too

quiz.explanation: Page 4 says Mo wants to act instead of always guessing. Page 7 says he is pleased that the game can include other things, not just animals.

quiz.prompt: Explain how Mo went from a quiet guesser to an actor with a new idea for the game.
quiz.rubric: not yet: names an animal without explaining Mo's quiet turn; with support: says Mo wanted to act and Sam let him, with prompting; independent: links Mo's wish to act, Sam's invitation, and Mo's umbrella idea that expands the game beyond animals
quiz.explanation: Page 4 gives Mo's wish, page 5 gives Sam's invitation, and pages 6 and 7 show how Mo adds a new kind of thing to guess.

activities.prompt: Arrange the changes in the rainy day game.

items.text: Sam suggests pretending to be animals.
Mo stays quiet during the penguin turn.
Sam pretends to be a teapot.

prompts: Would choosing another animal have given Mo what he wanted? Explain using his reason for being quiet.
Mo adds an umbrella to an animal game. What new category could you agree to add, and which rule must the actor still follow?

off_screen_prompt: Play silent guessing with a partner. Each person acts one animal and one household object, swapping jobs after every guess, then invent a new category together.
